targets.T14.17:
T14.17:
    name: Lines no command accepts produce a Java-equivalent syntax error instead of being silently dropped
    status: converging
    value: 0.0
    cost: 0.0
    acceptance:
    - For each diagram family, Rust tells apart a line that no Java command accepts (a syntax error, ported from Java's factory/command dispatch and error reporting) from a line whose Java command exists but is not yet implemented in Rust. The second kind is reported explicitly and never silently treated as valid output.
    - '`message_gap_em_legacy`, `message_gap_narrow_legacy` and the sequence cohort''s accepted invalid references are rejected with a Java-equivalent error outcome, and so are at least three held-out malformed inputs outside the golden corpus, in two or more families.'
    - No valid no-oracle or standing case newly becomes an error. The inventory of 'command exists in Java but not Rust' lines is measured and recorded, not hidden.
    context: |-
      Java PlantUML runs each diagram line through the diagram factory's command list. If no command accepts a line, the diagram is a syntax error: Java returns an error SVG with exit 200. In Rust, `parse_sequence` marks such a line as unconsumed and still returns a diagram, so the malformed command just disappears.

      On 2026-11-05 the sequence maker repaired its whitespace regex: `sequence_regex` now refuses EM SPACE and narrow NBSP separators, as Java's `Pattern2` `%s` does. Even so, `message_gap_em_legacy` and `message_gap_narrow_legacy` still render as successful diagrams, because the refused line falls through as unconsumed. Changing how unconsumed lines are handled globally inside a sequence-only packet would also reject commands that are valid but not yet supported, so this needs its own source-derived design. The same silent-drop pattern probably affects other families, and contributes to the invalid references Rust currently accepts (59 rejected / 20 accepted in the sequence cohort).
    tags:
    - parity
    - parser
    - negative-diagnostics
    origin: manual
    discovered: 2026-11-05
targets.T14.21:
T14.21:
    name: Diagram-type dispatch follows Java PSystemBuilder factory order, falling through on factory syntax errors
    status: identified
    value: 0.0
    cost: 0.0
    acceptance:
    - Rust dispatch uses the same factory order and syntax-error fall-through as Java's `PSystemBuilder`, traced from the source. No family-detection heuristic remains where Java uses fall-through.
    - The 13 misrouted sources listed in the sequence rejection candidate (`/Users/marcelo/Library/Caches/rustuml-sequence-rejection-dc438/candidate1/new-valid-errors.json`) render as their Java family, and so do at least three held-out mixed-case or direction-first inputs outside the golden corpus.
    - 'All 12,550 goldens are measured with the actual CLI before and after: no lost pass, no new valid-input error, and every family change is reported.'
    context: |-
      Java's `PSystemBuilder` tries each registered diagram factory in a fixed order and moves on to the next factory when one reports a syntax error. Rust's dispatcher picks one family up front, using heuristics.

      The sequence 🎯T14.17 candidate made "no registered sequence command accepts …" a real syntax error. Its replay (2026-11-05) then exposed 13 valid non-sequence sources that Rust misroutes to Sequence: class/description sources with mixed-case containers (`NoDe`) or a first line that is only a direction (`left to right direction`), and one state source with a stereotyped pseudostate. These sources were already wrong-family failures before the change. With strict sequence parsing they now fail with a CLI error.

      Source trace (sequence maker, 2026-11-05). Java's `PSystemBuilder` factory order is Welcome, Colors, Sequence, Class, Activity, Description, State, Activity3, and so on. `createPSystem` (lines 230–255) moves to the next factory when one returns a `PSystemError`, and merges the errors if every factory fails. Fall-through cannot be ported faithfully yet, because Rust's non-sequence factories accept any input. `class::parse_class` (class.rs:32–51) always returns `Ok(parser.finish())`, and `ClassParser::parse_line` (674–676) ignores every unrecognized line. Component and state behave the same way. A naive fall-through would let Class accept arbitrary malformed input and never reach Description or State. So this target depends on each family factory having a Java-equivalent command admission and syntax-error contract (the 🎯T14.17 work, per family). The 13 misrouted sources are a parent-approved recorded exception in the sequence 🎯T14.17 packet: they now fail with a CLI error instead of rendering as a Sequence diagram of the wrong family.
    tags:
    - parity
    - parser
    - dispatch
    origin: manual
    discovered: 2026-11-05

    name: TIM line continuation joins continued lines before diagram parsing, as Java does
    status: identified
    value: 0.0
    cost: 0.0
    acceptance:
    - TIM line-continuation joining is ported from the pinned Java preprocessor source and applied before diagram parsing.
    - Both retained line-continuation sources, plus at least two held-out continuation inputs outside the golden corpus (including continuations inside macros and themes), produce the same evaluated source as Java and the same whole output.
    - No previously passing no-oracle or standing case is lost.
    context: 'Two retained TIM sources pass their continued line (for example `second`) to the diagram parser as a separate line instead of joining it to the previous one: `tim-evaluated-event-stream/retained_checker_line_continuation.puml` and `tim-theme-post-expansion-source-identity/checker_line_continuation.puml`. Before the sequence 🎯T14.17 candidate this produced a wrong diagram. With strict sequence parsing it becomes a CLI syntax error. The fix belongs in the preprocessor (`preprocess/mod.rs`, about 2,900 lines; read it in full before editing), not in diagram parsers.'
    tags:

    origin: manual
